data.narrative:
Credo Semiconductor is a public-stage company in the Chips & Semiconductors sector, currently valued at approximately $35.8B following its 2022 IPO. The valuation analysis draws on a comparable universe of 3 public peers in the same sector and stage (Cerebras at $39.2B, Ouster at $2.3B, and Aeva Technologies at $1.1B), alongside a broader reference set of 8 private frontier-tech semiconductor companies.

The peer-median method is the applicable triangulation approach here. The median valuation across the three same-sector, same-stage comparables stands at $2.3B, with a range spanning $1.1B to $39.2B. A public-comp anchoring method using P/S multiples from broader semiconductor tickers (ALAB, NVDA, AMD)—which trade at a 21.0x sector median—cannot be applied without Credo's disclosed revenue figure, which is not available.

The triangulated valuation range supports $1.9B to $2.6B, centered at $2.3B. This analysis reflects meaningful uncertainty: the 15x spread between the lowest and highest peer ($1.1B to $39.2B) underscores the high dispersion typical of early-stage semiconductor ventures, where technical differentiation and market timing create outsized valuation variance. The reliance on a single applicable method further constrains confidence. Credo's current $35.8B public valuation sits substantially above this peer-derived range, warranting examination of revenue scale, margin profile, or market-share dynamics not captured in this comparable set.
